Joyful
joi´ful
adj. (full of gladness; rendering Hebrew samach, Greek chairo)
Joy with the intensive ending. Scripture's joyfulness is repeatedly commanded, which assumes it is not merely a temperament.

Biblical Definition

Joyful means full of gladness. The psalms command it corporately: “Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands” (Psa 100:1). Paul, writing from prison, reports being “exceeding joyful in all our tribulation” (2Co 7:4). Isaiah promises that God will make the outcasts “joyful in my house of prayer” (Isa 56:7), and Ecclesiastes counsels, “live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity” (Ecc 9:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines joyful as full of joy; very glad; exulting; and giving joy or pleasure.

expand to see more

JOYFUL, a. Full of joy; very glad; exulting.

2. Giving joy or pleasure; as joyful news; joyful days.

Key Scripture

Psa 100:1 — "A Psalm of praise. Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands."

2Co 7:4 — "Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation."

Isa 56:7 — "Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people."

Ecc 9:9 — "Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun."

Modern Corruption

Joy is waited on as a mood, and Scripture keeps commanding it — which means it is available to obedience and not only to circumstance.

expand to see more

2 Corinthians 7:4 refuses the assumption that joy waits on relief: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation. Not after it, not despite forgetting it — in it. Paul had just described being troubled on every side, without were fightings, within were fears. The joy and the fear occupy the same paragraph, which is more honest than either a religion that denies the fear or a realism that denies the joy.

Isaiah 56:7 attaches joy to a place and a people: even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer… for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people. The ones addressed are the foreigner and the eunuch — those who had assumed they were excluded. God does not merely admit them; He undertakes to make them joyful there.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew samach (H8055), to rejoice, be glad; rua (H7321), to shout, make a joyful noise; Greek chairo (G5463), to rejoice.

expand to see more

Hebrew samach (H8055) — to rejoice; Isaiah 56:7, Ecclesiastes 9:9, Psalm 5:11.

Hebrew rua (H7321) — to shout, raise a war cry or joyful noise; Psalm 100:1, 95:1.

Greek chairo (G5463) — to rejoice; Philippians 4:4, rejoice in the Lord alway.

Usage

"“Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands” — joy commanded corporately."

"“Exceeding joyful in all our tribulation” — in it, not after it."

"“Make them joyful in my house of prayer” — promised to those who assumed exclusion."
